title: Ζητήσεις καὶ εὑρήματα
description: Ten stories and dialogues about inquiry and discovery in the first-century Greek East: a sponge diver's ancient wreck, a physician tracing a fever to a dirty pool, a ploughman's buried silver, the capture of Syracuse weighed by a teacher, spies in a market harbour, a bear taken for a ghost, a month-long test of dreams, Democritus' atoms, the origin of the feast of Dedication, and the lost salt of Kition.

lessons.title: Τὸ πλοῖον ἐν τῷ βάθει
lessons.summary: Off Kythera the young sponge diver Koroibos of Kalymna finds an old wreck on the sea floor; with two other divers they bring up bronze vessels and figures and a small ivory throne, the shipowner Leodamas works out from the few jars left that the crew once threw most of the cargo overboard in a storm, and the divers land at Kalymna with their find.

lessons.title: Οἱ δύο παῖδες καὶ ἡ ἄψινθος
lessons.summary: In Colossae the poor widow Nikarete's two small sons fall ill with fever, burning eyes and sickness of the stomach; the physician Archagoras asks what they ate and drank, finds that they drank from a dirty pool and have small worms inside, gives them wormwood, which they spit out until he puts honey in it, puts clean oil into their eyes, and in a few days the boys are well again.

lessons.title: Ὁ θησαυρὸς ὑπὸ τὸ ἄροτρον
lessons.summary: Near Pergamon the farmer Melon, ploughing a field beside his olive grove with his son Thrasylos, strikes an old buried wall; digging closer to the grove they find a jar of uncoined silver and a stone with an engraved inscription, the village elders tell them a rich man hid it in the war of Mithridates, and the village marvels at the find.

lessons.title: Ἡ ἅλωσις τῶν Συρακουσῶν
lessons.summary: In Syracuse the teacher Leptines walks with his pupil Epikydes along the old walls and talks about the city's capture by Marcellus: how Archimedes' machines threw the mocking Romans into confusion, whether he really set their ships on fire with mirrors, how the city fell during a festival of Artemis, and how a raging soldier killed the old man; they weigh the stories and keep what is likely.

lessons.title: Οἱ ἐγκάθετοι ἐν τῷ ἐμπορίῳ
lessons.summary: In the market harbour of Attalia the purple merchant Glaukias finds that his rival Kteson always knows his prices first; the overseer Dromokleides suspects two new porters, tells a false price in front of them alone, and when Kteson uses it, he puts the porters under oath; they stand speechless, one slips away, the other confesses, and Kteson is driven out of the market.

lessons.title: Τὸ θηρίον τὸ ἄφαντον
lessons.summary: A young student from Kyzikos tells how he went to a Mysian village under Olympus where shepherds said an invisible spirit took their sheep; he walked the hills, found bear tracks and hair in a net he had spread out, followed them to a cave, and with the village elder Simos and the shepherds drove the bear away with fire and noise.

lessons.title: Περὶ τῶν ἐνυπνίων
lessons.summary: In Tarsus two pupils come to their teacher Eukles half asleep after a feast; Kleitos says dreams foretell what will happen, Onomastos says they come from wine and food; Eukles tells them to sober up and listen, and sets them a test: for a month each writes down his dreams every morning and later counts how many came true; few did, and the teacher concludes that a dream may come true by chance, but most come from the body.

lessons.title: Ἡ ἄτομος
lessons.summary: In a garden in Athens the pupil Nikomachos asks his teacher Charikles whether a loaf can be cut in half for ever; the teacher sets out the two views, Democritus' indivisible atom and Aristotle's endless division, shows him wine spreading through water and a wet cloak drying, and answers those who call such inquiries useless.

lessons.title: Ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἐγκαινίων
lessons.summary: In Alexandria the young Jew Tryphon, brought up in the law but now living like the Greeks of the gymnasium, tells his father Aristoboulos that the winter feast of Dedication is self-made worship because the law of Moses does not command it; his father sends him to the scribe of the house of prayer, who unwraps an old book and shows him how Judas Maccabeus cleansed and dedicated the temple, and Tryphon keeps the feast with his family.

lessons.title: Τὸ ἅλα τοῦ Κιτίου
lessons.summary: Near Kition in Cyprus the owner of the salt pans, Onasikypros, finds that his salt has fallen short for a second summer; with his overseer Timokreon he looks into each step of the work, from the sea water let into the shallow pans to the salt carried out in woven baskets, and they discover that winter storms have filled the channel from the sea with sand; the workers dig it out, and the next summer the salt is as plentiful as before.
